evidence.claim: TAL-15, the push notification service, blocks TAL-56 and is still in Backlog.
TAL-16, the Apple developer account and push certificate, blocks TAL-15 and is still open. This holds up TAL-56 indirectly.
TAL-31 is a Slack notification for paid invoices and is already Done. It overlaps only in part, so it is not a duplicate.

body.why: TAL-56 is Blocked because TAL-15 (Push notification service) is still in Backlog, and TAL-15 is itself waiting on TAL-16 (Apple developer account for push certificates), which is also open. The issue has a clear description and acceptance criteria, so the blockers are the only problem.
wouldChange: TAL-15 is done, which needs TAL-16 done first.
The link from TAL-15 to TAL-56 is removed, for example if push delivery is built inside TAL-56.

evidence.claim: The final decision from Security and Payments says Tally never stores card numbers or CVCs. Saved cards must use Stripe saved payment methods. This contradicts TAL-65.
TAL-65 has acceptance criteria, but they require saving the card number after the first payment, which is the behavior the decision forbids.

body.why: TAL-65 asks to store card numbers, but the final decision page Decision: we never store card numbers says Tally keeps only the Stripe payment method token. Building it as written would break that decision.
wouldChange: Rewrite TAL-65 to use Stripe saved payment methods and store only the payment method token, in line with the decision page.
Security and Payments formally reverse or amend the decision page Decision: we never store card numbers.

evidence.claim: TAL-9 covers authenticator-app one-time codes with enrolment via QR code, plus recovery codes and admin enforcement. That includes everything TAL-49 asks for (time-based codes, enrolment, code at sign-in). It is in progress.
TAL-49 asks for TOTP as a second sign-in step, with only two criteria: an enrolment flow and a code asked at sign-in.

body.why: TAL-49 is already covered by TAL-9, which is in progress. Both add authenticator-app one-time codes with enrolment and a code check at sign-in, and TAL-9 also covers recovery codes and admin enforcement. Call: Duplicate.
wouldChange: TAL-49 names work that TAL-9 does not cover, such as a different login surface or a non-authenticator-app method, which would make it Risky as a partial overlap.
TAL-9 is dropped or its scope is cut to exclude the sign-in code check, which would leave TAL-49 as Ready to Build.

evidence.claim: TAL-24 cached computed invoice totals to speed up the list page, shipped, then was reverted after totals went stale when line items changed.
TAL-68 has acceptance criteria (totals served from cache, list under one second) but none cover invalidation when line items change.
TAL-64 covers the same slow invoice list problem (6 seconds for over 10,000 invoices) and is still open, so it overlaps only in goal.

body.why: Risky: TAL-24 cached the same invoice totals in memcached and was reverted because totals went stale when line items changed. TAL-68 swaps in Redis and doesn't say how it avoids the same staleness.
wouldChange: Add an acceptance criterion and a plan for invalidating cached totals when line items change, which addresses the reason TAL-24 was reverted.
Confirm the Redis approach differs from TAL-24 in a way that prevents stale totals, then it can move to Ready to Build.

evidence.claim: TAL-2 is an earlier issue that queues dropped Stripe events when the webhook endpoint fails and retries them with exponential backoff. This is the same work as TAL-42.
TAL-42 asks to keep Stripe events lost during an outage and replay them automatically. This is the same problem and fix as TAL-2.
TAL-14 is an audit log pipeline that only shares the word event. It is not related work.

body.why: This is a Duplicate of TAL-2, which already covers storing Stripe events that fail while our endpoint is down and retrying them automatically. Both acceptance criteria in TAL-42 (no event lost, automatic replay) are covered by TAL-2's criteria.
wouldChange: TAL-42 needs something TAL-2 does not cover, such as replaying events after an outage longer than 24 hours or a manual replay tool. That would make it Risky because the overlap is only partial.
TAL-2 is closed as won't do or rejected. TAL-42 could then be Ready to Build.

evidence.claim: TAL-74 has a description and three acceptance criteria: full or partial credit, credit note linked to the invoice, invoice balance updated.
The decision page Decision: sent invoices are immutable says mistakes on sent invoices are corrected by issuing a credit note, which matches this issue.
TAL-69 only exports invoices and credit notes as CSV. It is related but does not cover issuing credit notes, so it is not a duplicate.

body.why: TAL-74 has a description and clear acceptance criteria, and nothing linked blocks it. The decision page Decision: sent invoices are immutable agrees with it, because it says mistakes on sent invoices are fixed by issuing a credit note.
wouldChange: A linked issue that must ship first, such as an unresolved credit note data model, would make this Blocked.
An earlier issue that already covers issuing credit notes from sent invoices would make this a Duplicate.
